title: Day 2: down -24% and weirdest ever day
author: Lumpy-Owl-7795
selftext:
Day 2 of my SPY 0DTE bot and unfortunately, I'm down 24% and at breakeven

  
This was my fault haha. This should not have happened if I just closed sooner. I saw a 25% profit but I decided to just leave, hoping for 30% haha. 27% turn into my -35% stop.

  
So new update -> I'm changing my stop to -30% instead of -35%. Then I will start taking profit at 25%, 50% and then 100%. 

Now before you say I told you so. I did not randomly build a bot and gave real cash. I have been testing this since Sep 18th. I started with $1k paper, now that has turned into $5k. a 400% profit. The bot still has 65%-win rate. I will send you proof all the trades + broker statements if you want to verify. 

This is not new and has happened b4, see the growth curve and you'd see there no linear growth here. As long as I have blown up, I'm fine: just a minor setback. This is long term!!! But this is so funny tho haha...

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: Posting the red day is good, but I'd be careful about changing the stop and take-profit rules right after one loss, because that tweaks the system to the last trade. Test the new -30% / 25-50-100% exit scheme on the same logged trades and on a new batch, and keep the old rule running in parallel on paper so you can compare. A 28-trade paper record with a 65% win rate is a small sample, and with 0DTE options a few trades can dominate the P&L, so I'd also look at the average win versus average loss and the worst day. Scheduled releases (CPI, FOMC) move 0DTE hard, and Cymetica's EventTrader (event timing for macro releases) is one source for tagging those days.

comments.author: ejpusa

Suggest: Go back to paper trading. You can then trade the exact opposite positions and collect more observable data.

Codex will explain why you are losing. And how to change your Model. The Astra + Codex Pipeline is where you want to be.

My math is in the Prediction Markets, but should also be applicable here.

Good luck, happy trading.

comments.author: Technical-Athlete-9
comments.body: But you just fitted the curve on the fly, incorporating the most recent sample, and you’re not trading the system but taking discretionary exits. So this experiment isn’t telling you if the bot can live trade what you saw in backtests. It’s just telling you if a pattern repeats two days in a row and that following rules can be hard.

replies.author: Technical-Athlete-9
replies.body: Actually I don’t know if that was curve fitting unless you backtested again. Maybe it was just introducing recency bias to the rules.
